newsitem.title: HUNGARY: IEB plans 12.5pct dividend, capital hikes.
newsitem.headline: IEB plans 12.5pct dividend, capital hikes.

text.p: Hungary's Inter-Europa Bank plans to pay 12.5 percent dividend or 1,250 forints a share on its 1996 results, IEB Chairman Laszlo Body said on Wednesday, quoted by the Hungarian news agency MTI-ECONEWS.
The bank paid a 12.5 percent dividend plus a 2.5 percent dividend premium last year.
Body said IEB's board of directors would propose to the annual shareholders' meeting on April 24, to pay a dividend of 1,250 forints for each share.
He added that shareholders would also vote on two planned capital increases.
The first move, which is to be financed from the bank's reserves, would double IEB's 2.8 billion forint capital by giving the bank's owners an extra share for each share currently held.
Body said the shareholders should also authorize the board of directors to carry out in early autumn a second capital rise, which is planned by the board to be worth 1.4 billion forints.
Part of these shares, with a total nominal value of 1.245 billion forints, would be offered publicly, but IEB shareholders would have a pre-emption right.

The remaining stocks of 158 million forints would be "B" series shares, MTI-ECONEWS said, adding that the "B" series ensured managerial positions and veto rights to the largest shareholder, Italy's Gruppo Bancario San Paolo SpA.
The "B" series stocks would maintain their 22.5 percent share in the registered capital after the capital increase, MTI-ECONEWS added.
Inter-Europa closed at 47,250 forints, up 1,700 forints, on the Budapest Stock Exchange.
